channel.title: Shreyas Korad — Writing
channel.description: Articles and insights on learning design, gamification, and L&D strategy.

item.title: Gamification fails at the moment of choice
item.description: Gamification works in rehearsal and fails at the moment of choice - the instant where the player decides between the new behavior and the familiar one. Most systems never design for that moment.

item.title: Invisible feedback loops are already shaping behavior
item.description: Every organization has feedback loops running whether or not anyone designed them. The ones that win are the ones people respond to - not the ones leaders announce.

item.title: Shared quests work only when teaching decisions improve
item.description: Quest mechanics fail when the underlying teaching decisions - what to practice, how to recover from failure, when to progress - remain unchanged. The mechanics are visible. The stagnation is invisible.

item.title: Gamification collapses when motivation design is weak
item.description: The Wikipedia paradox exposes a fault line in every workplace engagement program: people don't engage because you reward them. They engage because the activity itself returns something the reward cannot deliver.

item.title: Why delight belongs inside the core loop
item.description: Products that people love don't sprinkle delight on top of utility. They build emotional value into the mechanism itself - and the diagnostic for whether you've done it is brutally simple.

item.title: Gamification fails when it turns into surveillance or burnout
item.description: Disney's electronic whip, FarmVille's withering crops, and Yahoo Answers' point system share a structural failure: each was designed around what's easy to measure, not around what sustains the behavior the designers actually wanted.
